defect_leakage.title: ExplanationWrong[CorrectChoice] Non-Empty
defect_leakage.earliest_possible_detection: At content-authoring time — the template engine should never have emitted ExplanationWrong fields at the CorrectChoice position. Second: during CAQS §1.6 certification, EV8 compliance should have been verified before assigning 'Certified' state.
defect_leakage.why_not_caught_earlier: 1) No automated pre-certification EV8 scan existed — the ExplanationValidator skipped non-empty slots silently (line 180 gap). 2) Governance guard Rule 2 was activated AFTER thousands of items were already Certified. 3) Sub-agent instructions for Wave 1 certification did not include 'clear EW[CC]' step (added from Wave 2 onwards). 4) Template-based bulk authoring filled all 4 EW slots regardless of CorrectChoice — a systemic design flaw in the authoring pipeline, not an oversight.

recurrence_timeline.action: Clear + add EV8 instruction to templates
Confirmed 0 Certified DL-008 via Function constructor

defect_leakage.current_state: RESOLVED — 0 actual Certified DL-008. The 67-count in SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-24 was a DL-029 forward-scan artifact. All 2,500 items verified clean via Function constructor parse (S801/S802).

defect_leakage.title: Misassigned Choice Explanations
defect_leakage.severity: High (explanation text describes wrong choice — learners receive misleading feedback)

detection_points.method: Rotation-group forward-scan → refuted by within-object extraction

defect_leakage.earliest_possible_detection: During CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification — the Correctness dimension check should verify that each ExplanationWrong field semantically describes its assigned choice. An automated lexical-overlap check between EW text and choice text could flag low-relevance assignments.
defect_leakage.why_not_caught_earlier: 1) No automated semantic-alignment validator exists — this is inherently an NLP/semantic check. 2) DL-016 metadata-content divergence creates scanning false positives — the metadata-block ChoiceA-D text differs from the learner-facing Choices.A-D, so EW text that describes the learner's choice appears to describe the metadata choice instead. 3) Most DL-010 findings were actually DL-016 scan artifacts — the EW text was correct for the primary block, but scans read the wrong block.
defect_leakage.current_state: OPEN — scoped at 125 true DL-010 across 5 packs (reduced from initial 2,038 raw findings). Mostly mechanical fixes (incorrect-answer calculation summaries in EW slots). Frequent false-positive cascades from DL-016/DL-029 scan methodology.

defect_leakage.title: Metadata-Block Choice Divergence (Dual-Block Architecture Shift)
defect_leakage.severity: HIGH — ExplanationWrong fields describe the +1 offset item's topic, not the learner-facing choices. Learners see feedback about a completely different topic.

detection_points.gate: Tier 0 false-alarm investigation (initially stem-choice mismatch false positive)

detection_points.method: Single-object architecture verification + full-section EW audit

defect_leakage.earliest_possible_detection: At content-authoring time — the template engine's metadata block and content block should be verified for alignment before any items are emitted. A pre-certification structural scan comparing metadata ChoiceA-D vs. content Choices.A-D would catch this.
defect_leakage.why_not_caught_earlier: 1) Architecture was not understood as dual-block until Session 64 — prior scans treated the file as single-object, missing the metadata-content divergence. 2) The defect originated from the same template-rotation pipeline that produced DL-012 clones — the metadata block carried stale rotation-template choices. 3) Scan tools read from the wrong block (flat 'ChoiceA' regex vs. 'Choices.A' path-aware nesting), producing false 'stem-choice mismatch' alarms instead of the actual DL-016 finding. 4) Section E was later confirmed as SINGLE-OBJECT (S805) — the +1 shift was a different mechanism: EW text was genuinely misassigned to offset-distributed QIDs in the rotation group, not a metadata vs. content block divergence.

defect_leakage.title: CorrectChoice Answer-Key Errors
defect_leakage.severity: CRITICAL (wrong answer marked correct — highest learner-safety risk)

detection_points.method: Independent re-derivation of all Certified items' answer keys

defect_leakage.earliest_possible_detection: During CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification — the Correctness dimension REQUIRES independent derivation of the correct answer before approving the stored CorrectChoice. If the certification workflow had actually performed this step, all 5 would have been caught before certification.
defect_leakage.why_not_caught_earlier: 1) Certification was performed by sub-agents that did NOT independently derive answers — they verified ExplanationCorrect text but accepted the stored CorrectChoice letter as given. 2) The template rotation group assigned CorrectChoice letters by position rather than by verification against choice text. 3) Three of five errors were conceptual design errors (template assigned CC to wrong letter) where ExplanationCorrect text was correct — sub-agents reviewing the explanation would see correct reasoning and approve, not realizing the CC letter didn't match.

recurrence_timeline.action: All 5 items fixed, EW[new_CC] cleared, EC updated where needed

defect_leakage.current_state: RESOLVED — all 5 items fixed. defect_leakage.title: Definition-Match Difficulty Inflation (Systematic)
defect_leakage.severity: HIGH (systematic — ~500 items labeled Moderate that test Bloom's Remember/Understand)
defect_leakage.earliest_possible_detection: During CAQS §1.6 Dimension 3 (Difficulty Calibration) and Dimension 5 (Blueprint Alignment). The certification workflow should verify that difficulty labels match cognitive demand — not accept template-assigned labels at face value.
defect_leakage.why_not_caught_earlier: 1) Template-rotation authoring pipeline assigned difficulty by position in rotation group (Easy, Moderate, Moderate, Difficult, Moderate) without cognitive assessment. 2) Certification sub-agents did not challenge difficulty labels — they accepted the stored label. 3) No automated Jaccard-overlap check between stem and correct-answer choice exists to flag definition-match items. 4) DifficultyCalibrationValidator does not exist as a module in the validator pipeline.
defect_leakage.current_state: OPEN — scoped, not remediated. Deferred to post-certification difficulty recalibration phase. Companion defect DL-032 (Case Bank: all 420 case items labeled 'Moderate').

root_causes.title: No Pre-Certification Automated Structural Scan
root_causes.description: The certification pipeline (CAQS §1.6 six-dimension verification) was executed by sub-agents that verified ExplanationCorrect text quality but did NOT run automated structural scans for EV8 compliance (DL-008), field presence (DL-021, DL-025/026), field uniqueness (DL-013), metadata-content alignment (DL-016), or answer-key correctness (DL-030). Items entered 'Certified' state without passing any automated pre-certification gate.
root_causes.evidence: The ExplanationValidator (only tool in the validator pipeline relevant to EW fields) had a line-180 gap that silently skipped non-empty EW[CC] slots. The validator was never fixed until AFTER thousands of items were certified. Governance guard Rule 2 was active but only blocked WRITE-TIME DL-008 — it did not scan EXISTING Certified items.
root_causes.fix_status: S802-S803: AM-1/AM-2 scan methodology standards established. Function constructor parse adopted as authoritative. S725: scan methodology standard with 3 approved methods and 8 forbidden.

root_causes.title: Concurrent Session Overwrites — No File-Lock or Session Coordination
root_causes.description: Multiple sessions operated on the same pack files simultaneously without write-lock coordination. The DL-019 incident — where the DL-013 certification wave wrote to Pack C/D from a pre-DL-008-remediation disk snapshot, silently overwriting 432 cleared items — is the canonical case. This is a process defect, not a tooling defect.
root_causes.evidence: DL-019: 432 items in Pack C (243) and Pack D (189) restored to pre-clear state. DL-028: DL-013 remediation tooling created new empty slots while other agents were certifying the same sections. Session 53 acknowledged this risk and established the T0→Tmid→Tend checkpoint system, but implementation was documentation-only — no file-lock protocol deployed.
root_causes.fix_status: Documented in SESSION53 but not yet implemented as active runtime governance. AGENTS.md §4 mandates backup-before-write but no session-level lock coordination exists.

root_causes.title: Scan Methodology Fragility — DL-029 Forward-Scan False Positives
root_causes.description: Multiple scan methodologies used a 'forward-scan from QuestionID to find CorrectChoice' approach. In all 5 packs, CorrectChoice appears BEFORE QuestionID in the JSON object (confirmed S801). Forward-scanning systematically grabs the NEXT item's CorrectChoice, producing ~75% false-positive rates. This created phantom defect counts that consumed entire remediation sessions while real defects went undetected.
impacted_defects: DL-008 (67 phantom Certified → 0 actual), DL-010 (false positive cascades in S500-S507), DL-016 (scan artifact confusion), DL-026 (count instability 632→1,005→5-agent dispute)
root_causes.evidence: SESSION_STATUS_2026-07-24 reported 67 Certified DL-008. Session 92 found 672. S801 Function constructor parse found 0 actual. The 67 and 672 counts were both DL-029 artifacts. The forward-scan methodology also caused the Pack B DL-008 false positive (111 items, zero actual) and the Pack D DL-008 discrepancy (342 per S700 vs. 10 per SESSION_STATUS → 20 actual).
root_causes.fix_status: S802: All methodologies now require within-object CC extraction (Function constructor parse or brace-matched object-boundary parse). S725: Scan Methodology Standard with 8 forbidden approaches (including any forward-scan). AGENTS.md §5 mandates cross-check of scan results against raw file/line evidence.

root_causes.title: Template Engine Without Quality Gates — Systemic Defect Injection at Authoring Time
root_causes.description: The bulk-authoring template engine produced systematic defects that only became visible when items entered certification. The template: 1) Filled all 4 ExplanationWrong slots regardless of CorrectChoice (DL-008), 2) Assigned difficulty labels by rotation position, not cognitive assessment (DL-031, DL-032), 3) Left one distractor slot per item empty as a 'secondary CC slot' in the rotation (DL-025/DL-026), 4) Assigned CorrectChoice letters by rotation cycle, not verification (DL-030), 5) Stored stale metadata-block choices from prior rotation templates (DL-016). Every defect class traces to the template pipeline.
root_causes.evidence: DL-012 documented the 5-item rotation group template producing 140 clones. DL-013 documented 2,587 boilerplate fields from the same template. DL-026 root cause analysis identified the rotation template's 'secondary CC slot' artifact. DL-030 root cause was the template assigning CC by position, not verification. The S311/S313 'EW Factory' approach (explanations authored at creation time with quality gates) was the explicit response to this root cause.
root_causes.fix_status: S311 'EW Factory' quality standard adopted for new content authoring. Requires: EC ≥ 400 chars, EW ≥ 100 chars, DL-008/026/013 compliance at creation. Domain E modernization content (S313-S316) applied this retroactively. Existing packs still carry template artifacts in non-Certified sections.

root_causes.title: Validator Coverage Gap — Line-173/180 Silent Skips
root_causes.description: The ExplanationValidator (the only structural validator for EW fields) had two critical gaps: line 173 silently skipped undefined fields (`if (!val) return;`) and line 180 silently skipped non-empty EW[CC] fields (pre-patch). These gaps meant the validator chain that items passed before certification was literally blind to DL-008, DL-018, DL-021, DL-025, and DL-026.
root_causes.evidence: ExplanationValidator.js: line 173 (`if (!val) return;`) skips both undefined and empty-string fields. Line 180 gap (fixed 2026-07-23 by Agent 1) previously ONLY warned about non-empty EW fields, never flagged an error. The governance guard Rule 2 was reactive — it blocked NEW certifications with DL-008 but could not catch items already Certified.
root_causes.fix_status: Line 180 gap fixed (2026-07-23 Agent 1). Line 173 gap remains — validator still silently skips absent/empty distractor EW fields. AM-1/AM-2 scan methodology standards now use Function constructor parse for within-object verification. Governance guard Rule 2 active for write-time blocking.

top_3_root_causes.impact: Items entered 'Certified' state without detection of DL-008 (EV8), DL-025/026 (empty distractor slots), DL-013 (boilerplate), DL-021 (missing fields), DL-031 (difficulty inflation), or DL-030 (wrong answer keys). Every other root cause was downstream of this one — if the pre-certification scan existed, template artifacts would have been caught before certification, and concurrent-session overwrites would have been detectable via count comparison.
top_3_root_causes.fix: AM-1/AM-2 scan methodology standards (S725), governance guard Rule 2 enforcement, within-object Function constructor parse adopted as authoritative
top_3_root_causes.sessions_consumed: ~15 sessions wasted on post-hoc defect discovery + remediation that pre-cert scanning would have eliminated

top_3_root_causes.cause: Template-based bulk authoring without quality gates
top_3_root_causes.impact: The 5-item rotation template systematically injected DL-008 (all 4 EW slots filled), DL-025/026 (secondary CC slot left empty), DL-013 (boilerplate distractor text), DL-016 (+1 metadata-content offset), DL-030 (CC assigned by position), and DL-031 (difficulty by position) into every section it touched. These defects were not introduced by remediation agents — they were present in the original authoring, undiscovered for weeks, and then surfaced only after items became 'Certified'.

The Pack D DL-008 discrepancy (342 vs. 10) consumed multiple sessions in count reconciliation. The S500-S507 DL-010 false alarms were all DL-016/DL-029 artifacts.

summary.path_to_prevention: 1) Install a pre-certification automated scan that runs ALL structural checks (EW field presence, EV8 compliance, field uniqueness, metadata-content alignment) before any item transitions to Certified. 2) Adopt the S311 'EW Factory' quality standard for all new content and retroactively apply to existing non-Certified sections. 3) Eliminate all forward-scan methodologies — use only within-object CC extraction (Function constructor parse). 4) Implement session-level file-lock coordination to prevent DL-019 concurrent-write overwrites.
summary.s200_context: SESSION200 found 89.5% readiness failure rate (34 of 38 Domain E seeds had 2+ concurrent defects). This S201 analysis confirms the root causes: template artifacts (DL-008/013/026/031) present at creation, no pre-cert scan to catch them, and scan methodology fragility creating phantom defect counts that misdirected remediation resources.
